messages:
Ana: Quick sync on rerank endpoint spec — focusing on top_k behavior, truncation strategy, and score normalization for the Q2 roadmap. Need clear launch gates and a minimal request contract by EOD Thurs.
Michael: :eyes: can we avoid forcing clients to pre-truncate? customers want predictable payload sizes but also stable ordering.
Devon: I think we need two orthogonal knobs: client_top_k (what they ask for) and server_return_k (what we actually return after truncation/backpressure). Allows us to enforce size limits without breaking client expectations.
Sarah: +1 from CS — enterprise customers asked for guaranteed monotonicity (if item A > B in score, order shouldn't flip after we normalize). They care about tie-break determinism too.
Michael: normalization options we discussed: softmax (good for soft probabilities), min-max (preserves relative gaps), z-score (unstable across batches). For rerank we probably want a monotonic transform that preserves ordering and is comparable across requests.
Jordan: tech constraints: runtime can apply a per-request affine scaling + clamp cheaply on GPU. Softmax across many candidates is more expensive because of exp/scan. If we pre-truncate to N then apply softmax it’s manageable.
Ana: Proposal: default behavior = 1) accept candidates array (ids + raw model_scores), 2) server applies configured truncate_policy (drop|pad|compress) to respect max_payload_tokens, 3) apply normalization mode = none|minmax|softmax (default=minmax), 4) return top_k as requested but capped to service_max_k.
Devon: Example request shape (proposal):
```
POST /v1/rerank
{
  'query': 'how to bake sourdough',
  'candidates': [ {'id':'c1','score': 0.23}, {'id':'c2','score': -0.1}, ... ],
  'top_k': 10,
  'truncate_policy': 'drop' // drop oldest candidates to meet size limits
}
```
Sarah: For rollout: CS wants an opt-in beta for 3 enterprise tenants, telemetry on score shifts, and a way to pin to pre-rollout behavior.
Michael: Launch gates I care about: unit tests for ordering invariants, deterministic tie-breaker, perf regression <5% p95 CPU/GPU, latency SLO for rerank path p95 <40ms on 8k candidate batch, and quotas for worst-case payload.
Jordan: Ops asks: add per-tenant normalization config (so enterprise can request raw scores back or request per-customer calibration), and logs that show before/after score distributions.
Ana: Customer-driven asks collected: 1) enforce top_k semantics (client-visible), 2) deterministic ordering & tie-breaks, 3) normalization that is comparable across requests, 4) truncation modes, 5) beta flag + telemetry. Prioritization: must-have = deterministic ordering + truncate_policy + service_max_k enforcement; should-have = per-tenant normalization config; nice-to-have = auto-calibration (learned mapping).
Michael: Edge cases: 1) candidates with identical scores -> stable sort by id, 2) negative/very large magnitude scores -> clamp before normalize, 3) streaming rerank (paging) -> require cursor that includes normalization seed.
Devon: Backpressure approach: if request_bytes > limit then apply truncate_policy='compress' first (dense repr), then 'drop'. Need an internal metric for dropped_fraction per-tenant.
Ana: Docs/action items: - Product to publish minimal API contract + examples (Ana) - Eng-ML to propose normalization algorithm and perf tradeoffs (Michael) - Runtime to implement truncate_policy and service_max_k with deterministic stable sort (Devon) - CS to pick beta tenants and define eval prompts (Sarah)
Sarah: I'll coordinate with pricing/legal for tenant opt-in and data retention notes.
product-bot: Created a follow-up ticket #PLAT-3721 for "rerank: truncate_policy + normalization" and assigned to @Devon.
Ana: Quick decision needed: default normalization = minmax, tie-breaker = id stable sort, service_max_k = 100. Objections?
Michael: fine with minmax as default for now, we'll add notes that softmax is available for probabilistic downstreams.
Devon: agree on stable id tie-breaker. I'll draft the API contract.
Ana: Great — aim to have PR with contract + tests by Wed EOD. We'll review in product sync Thursday. :rocket:
